articles.title: Intelligence predicts charitable giving and voting in massive Swedish study
articles.summary: A massive analysis of Swedish administrative records reveals that higher cognitive abilities strongly predict prosocial behaviors. Individuals with higher general intelligence are consistently more likely to donate to charity, vote in elections, and buy environmentally friendly vehicles.

articles.title: Your posture may change how much pain you feel
articles.summary: There may be a physical reason lying down feels good when you’re hurting. Pain sensitivity was modestly lower while lying flat, possibly because more blood returns to the chest and activates the body’s pressure sensors.

articles.title: Extraversion is linked to faster relief from depressive symptoms
articles.summary: During psychiatric treatment, a patient's personality and depression symptoms change in tandem. A new study reveals that high neuroticism slows recovery across multiple symptoms, while extraversion and agreeableness may help patients bounce back faster.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
articles.summary: The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture. Scientists suggest this change could be an evolutionary adaptation that helps older adults develop wisdom and share decades of knowledge with younger generations.

articles.title: Scientists find a way to fight Alzheimer’s brain damage without removing toxic tau
articles.summary: Scientists have found a promising way to protect the brain from Alzheimer’s-related damage by blocking immune cells that contribute to the destruction of neurons. In mice, the treatment preserved roughly 40% more tissue in memory centers and improved memory, even without removing harmful tau protein buildup.

articles.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup. The findings reveal a potential new way to prevent early brain damage and could pave the way for treatments that mimic this natural defense.

articles.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours

articles.title: To Keep or Not to Keep: Learning KV Cache Retention in Disaggregated LLM Serving Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disaggregated \textsc{LLM} serving separates prefill and decode across node pools, placing a network fabric between \textsc{KV}-cache computation and consumption. This breaks a key assumption of classical cache policies: a miss no longer incurs only local recomputation, but also network transfer to the decode node. Likewise, admitting a block to the global cache requires an additional transfer, so poor retention decisions waste both memory and bandwidth. articles.title: Interaction-Gated Time-Frequency Learning for Parameter-Efficient PPG-Based Heart Rate Estimation
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.28693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) enables low-cost and non-invasive heart rate (HR) monitoring but remains sensitive to waveform distortion, physiological variability, and measurement interference. Temporal waveform characteristics and frequency-domain periodicity provide complementary information for HR estimation; however, effectively exploring and integrating these representations within a compact model remains challenging. This paper proposes TF-IG, a parameter-efficient interaction-gated time-frequency learning framework for PPG-based HR estimation
